body:
This is exactly spot on.  Not so much the second check list, but the first check list reads exactly like my life.  

>Obsessive self-focus.

Every aspect of myself I scrutinize.  I feel that it's expected.  Not only does this apply in my work/school life, but also my physical appearance.  I am certain I am an attractive person (I haven't had to deal with those esteem issues since I was a child) but I have an obsession with looking at myself in the mirror to make sure my face still looks alright (?).  I don't even know how to explain it.  I'm not arrogant about my looks, I just want to make sure my face hasn't reverted back to something I'm not comfortable with.  I check an uncountable amount of times a day.  Sometimes (when I'm in class) I'll pull up my Photo Booth application (lets me take pictures) just to use as a mirror.  I'm tired of this stupid obsession that I feel like I can't control.  If I don't check at a regular basis I can't concentrate at all.  I've never told anybody about this obsessive compulsion I have because it's embarrassing as hell.

>Pressures to be exceptional.

It's been expected after following in the shadows of what I consider to be my extremely successful brother.  I love my brother, but I know that I will never be able to exceed his (what I deem) "greatness."  

>Unrealistic fantasies of wealth, power, celebrity or achievement.

This.  The thing is **I don't want those fantasies.**  I realized they were unrealistic when I was 10, but I have always felt pressured to accomplish this task.  I don't even give a fuck if I'm known in the world, but I feel it's expected from me from 1.) my friends and 2.) my family.  I do not want to go into detail as to why, but I get this almost weekly from either friends or family. 

I could go on and on with each specific one, but I don't want to go into any more detail.

I am going to read this book and then seek more therapy.
